plan: To preserve capital, sell all leveraged ETFs: SOXL, SPAL, and MUU.
Exit SMCI as it is below its stop and flagged for sale.
Trim SMH to 3% and QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration and address sell/trim flags.
Increase SPY to 25% for broad index exposure and stability.

conservative.read: This conservative plan targets around 1.5% per month, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by cutting leveraged ETFs and trimming concentrated positions. Expect lower volatility and smaller drawdowns, but also more modest returns.

plan: For risk-first growth, trim SOXL to 3%, SPAL to 1%, and MUU to 2% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure.

Trim QQQI to 20% to address the sell flag and reduce concentration.

balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for around 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding to strong broad index and quality tech names. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, with a blend of growth and stability.

plan: For aggressive growth, increase SOXL to 6%, SPAL to 6%, and MUU to 6% to lean into leveraged ETFs.

Trim QQQI to 15% to shift focus from income to growth.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware that this mode carries substantially higher risk, including larger potential drawdowns and daily decay/rebalancing effects of leveraged ETFs. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: To prioritize income, sell all leveraged ETFs: SOXL, SPAL, and MUU.
Exit SMCI and SMH completely to reduce high-beta tech exposure.
Increase QQQI to 30% to boost monthly distributions.
Add to SPY, increasing it to 25%, for broad market stability and lower drawdown.

income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month, aiming to park cash for yield. It significantly reduces high-beta and leveraged positions, favoring income-generating ETFs and broad index exposure. While prioritizing low drawdown and reliable income, remember that distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in market selloffs.
